content:
Hilary Swank is shaking off the criticism she’s received for getting pregnant with her third child at age 52.

Appearing on the British daytime talk show “This Morning” on Tuesday, Swank urged those critical of older women having children to “get with the times.”

“By the way, you’re [considered] geriatric, I think, at 34,” she said. “People are living so much longer, you know, and so many women are wanting to wait until later. It’s becoming quite a normal thing to have children later.”

A two-time Oscar winner for “Boys Don’t Cry” and “Million Dollar Baby,” Swank confirmed in a social media post last month that she and husband Philip Schneider are expecting their third child in December. The couple are already parents of 3-year-old twins, Aya and Ohm.

Swank’s announcement drew a polarized response on social media, with some users blasting the actor for her “selfish” and “irresponsible” decision.

The news was even the subject of a segment on “The Bobby Bones Show,” a nationally syndicated country music radio show based out of Tennessee, last month. The show’s hosts were divided, with one proclaiming: “That doesn’t seem right, healthy. That doesn’t seem safe.”

In her “This Morning” appearance, Swank acknowledged she spent much of her 20s and 30s focused on her pursuit of a Hollywood career.

“My career really was a baby of mine that I wanted to give to, and I didn’t want distractions,” she explained. “I wanted to give to that, and now I have both. I just feel so blessed; I feel so grateful and I love it, more than anything.”

So far, Swank doesn’t appear to have any intention of slowing down. She recalled working “18-hour days” on the fourth and final season of “Yellowjackets,” which premieres Friday.

“I had two body doubles because they couldn’t work overtime,” she quipped, “but the pregnant geriatric lady could!”

Two people who share Swank’s excitement for her pregnancy are her children.

“[Aya and Ohm] keep saying, ‘When’s the baby coming? When’s the baby coming?’ And I say, ‘Christmastime,’” the actor said. “And they wake up pretty much every morning, saying, ‘Is it Christmas yet?’ They’re so excited.”
